title: Platform systems & services: ops playbook, runbooks, dashboards and roadmap (Q3 2026)
author: Daniel Kim
content:
Summary:

This page consolidates the operational playbook for Platform Systems & Services: inventory, ownership, critical dashboards and alerts, runbooks for the most common incidents, short-term roadmap (Q3 2026) and team wiki pointers for onboarding and recurring how-tos. Intended audience: Platform engineers, SREs, oncall rotation, and platform-focused SEs.

1) Intro and purpose

- Purpose: one canonical reference for operating platform components that support Redwood inference (serving runtime, routing, caching, orchestration, observability pipeline).
- Scope: platform infra services (request-router, inference-runtime, kv-cache, edge-gateway, metrics-pipeline, autoscaler), dashboards, alerts, and runbooks.

2) Systems & services inventory (owners & SLIs)\n
| Service | Primary owner | Secondary | Location | Key SLIs / SLOs | Criticality |
|---|---|---|---|---:|---|
| request-router | platform-routing (team) | eng-platform | prod-cluster-1 / multi-region | request success rate >= 99.9% (30d), p95 latency <= 80ms | P0 |
| inference-runtime | serving-runtime | eng-serving-runtime | dedicated-gpu-pools | model inference success >= 99.5%, p95 token latency <= 120ms | P0 |
| kv-cache | infra-cache | eng-platform | redis-cluster-1 | cache hit rate >= 70% for prefix requests | P1 |
| edge-gateway | edge-team | platform-network | global-edge | TLS errors < 0.01% | P0 |
| metrics-pipeline | observability | eng-platform | prometheus/grafana/kafka | metrics ingest lag < 10s, loss < 0.05% | P0 |
| autoscaler | platform-scaling | eng-sre | control-plane | scale failure rate < 0.1% | P1 |

Notes: production means clusters labeled prod-* across us-west-2, eu-west-1. Primary owners are required to maintain dashboards and alerts listed below.

3) Dashboards & key panels (owners must keep these up to date)

- Global Platform Overview (Grafana): owned by eng-platform
  - Panels: overall error rate (by service), request rate (RPS), p50/p95/p99 latency per service, GPU utilization (per pod), queue depth for inference requests.
  - Critical grouping: inference-runtime, request-router, metrics-pipeline.
- Inference Runtime Dashboard (Grafana): owned by serving-runtime
  - Panels: token throughput, per-model latency histograms, KV cache miss ratio, GPU memory usage, CUDA kernel failure counts.
- Router & Edge Dashboard (Grafana): owned by platform-routing
  - Panels: upstream 5xx rate, TLS handshake errors, connection churn, routing fallback counts.
- Observability Pipeline Dashboard: owned by observability
  - Panels: prometheus scrape success, kafka consumer lag (metrics-pipeline), alertmanager health, metric cardinality trend.

Example panels to validate after deploy:
- p95 latency panel shows service.latency_bucket{le!="+Inf"} derived p95 via histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, service)).

4) Alerts & thresholds (must be actionable and owned)

- alert: Platform_HighErrorRate
  - expr: sum(rate(requests_total{job=~"(request-router|inference-runtime)" ,status=~"5.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(requests_total[5m])) > 0.001
  - for: 5m
  - severity: page
  - summary: "Elevated 5xx rate across platform services"
  - runbook: follow 'High error rate' runbook below.

- alert: Inference_HighLatency_P95
  - expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(inference_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, model)) > 0.12
  - for: 3m
  - severity: page
  - summary: "Inference runtime p95 latency > 120ms"

- alert: MetricsPipeline_Lag
  - expr: kafka_consumer_lag{consumer_group=~"metrics-pipeline"} > 10000
  - for: 2m
  - severity: page
  - summary: "Metrics pipeline lag (observability ingestion)"

- alert: KVCache_HitRateLow
  - expr: increase(kv_cache_hits_total[10m]) / (increase(kv_cache_hits_total[10m]) + increase(kv_cache_misses_total[10m])) < 0.5
  - for: 10m
  - severity: ticket
  - summary: "Low cache hit rate for KV cache"

Alert design guidelines:
- Page alerts for system-wide or service-critical failure modes (SLO jeopardy).
- Ticket alerts for degradation that can be mitigated during business hours.
- Each alert must include: responsible team label, runbook link, and escalation policy via PagerDuty service.

5) Runbooks (top incidents)

A) High error rate (platform-wide 5xx spike)

- Trigger: Platform_HighErrorRate page alert fires.
- PagerDuty: platform-sre PD service (rotation lead).
- Steps:
  1. Acknowledge the alert in PagerDuty and create an incident in the incident tracker template.
  2. Check Global Platform Overview dashboard: which service(s) have elevated 5xx? Filter by service and region.
  3. If concentrated in request-router or edge-gateway: check recent config change (check repo: infra/networking-configs, last commits) and load balancer health.
  4. If concentrated in inference-runtime: check model rollout flags (feature-flag service) and recent model swaps.
  5. Collect logs: use centralized log search (kibana/elastic): query status:5xx and correlate with request_id.
  6. If root cause is downstream (e.g., model container OOM): scale up replica count or restart failing pods per restart checklist.
  7. If root cause is traffic surge: activate throttling policy on request-router (route policy page) to protect runtime and enable graceful degradation (fallback to smaller model).
  8. Post-mitigation: close incident after 2x consecutive 5m windows below alert threshold and run RCA.

B) Inference runtime high latency (p95 > 120ms)

- Trigger: Inference_HighLatency_P95 page alert fires.
- Steps:
  1. Confirm scope: check per-model panels to see if single model or all models affected.
  2. Check GPU utilization and kernel errors on GPU nodes (nvidia-smi and node exporter metrics).
  3. Check KV cache hit ratio; low hit rate can increase token latencies.
  4. If GPU saturation: trigger autoscaler to add capacity (run: kubectl scale --replicas=<n> deploy/inference-runtime --namespace=prod). See autoscaler runbook for safe scaling thresholds.
  5. If model-specific regression: roll back to previous model version (note: follow model-rollout policy).
  6. If transient spike: enable short-term request queue shedding policy at router.
  7. After resolution: schedule model performance review and consider profiling job.

C) Observability ingestion lag

- Trigger: MetricsPipeline_Lag
- Steps:
  1. Validate consumer lag per topic and consumer group. If lag > 50k, page oncall.
  2. Check Grafana for increased cardinality or bursty scrapes.
  3. Restart metrics-consumer pods if consumer is stuck, with careful rollout (one pod at a time).
  4. If issues persist: increase consumer instances and scale Kafka partition assignment.

6) How-tos (common operational tasks)

- How to add a dashboard panel (Grafana):
  1. Create panel in the dev/grafana folder in the dashboards repo.
  2. Use templating vars: $service, $region. Provide panel description and intended alerts.
  3. Submit PR to grafana-dashboards repo. Tag primary owner in reviewers.
  4. After merge, verify in staging and then sync to prod via grafonnet CI job.

- How to tune an alert threshold:
  1. Check historical metric distribution (last 30d) using Grafana.
  2. Compute expected false positive rate for chosen threshold. Target <= 2 false pages/month for platform-wide alerts.
  3. Update Prometheus rule, include rationale in PR description, add test query, and document in alerts changelog.

- Onboarding a new service to Platform monitoring:
  1. Provision service-specific scrape configs (prometheus) and register service with observability team.
  2. Create a minimal dashboard with error rate and latency panels and link runbook.
  3. Add SLO definition to the SLO registry and schedule SLO burn-rate alerts.

7) Roadmap & initiatives (Q3 2026 priorities)

- Q3 objectives (owner: eng-platform):
  - Reduce platform P95 inference latency 10% by improved batching and default model config (milestone end of Aug).
  - Stabilize metrics pipeline: reduce ingestion loss to <0.02% (milestone mid-Sep).
  - Dashboard & alerting cleanup: remove 120 stale alerts and reclassify noisy ones (milestone end of Sep).
  - Launch runbook automation for common fixes (automated cache flush, scaler runbook) (milestone Sep 30).

Timeline (high level):
- Jul: finalize alert rationalization and runbook templates.
- Aug: deploy batching improvements to canary clusters and measure p95 delta.
- Sep: roll out observability pipeline fixes and automated mitigation playbooks.

8) Retrospective highlights (last quarter)

- Major incidents: two P0 incidents related to observability ingestion (May, Jun). Root cause: Kafka partition misconfiguration + bursty metric cardinality. Action items: automated partition rebalance script; cardinality budget alerts (done).
- Oncall feedback: alert fatigue from minor model rollout errors. Action: stricter alert thresholds for model-specific non-SLO impacting errors and improved runbook for model rollbacks (in progress).

9) Ownership, escalation and contact list

- Primary oncall PD services by category:
  - platform-sre (pager: +1-555-0101) - covers platform infra, routers, autoscaler.
  - serving-runtime (pager: +1-555-0202) - covers inference runtime and model rollouts.
  - observability (pager: +1-555-0303) - covers metrics-pipeline, logging.

- Slack channels: #platform-oncall, #serving-runtime, #observability. Use channel + PD for incident comms.

10) Post-incident process (RCA expectations)

- Every P0/P1 incident must have an RCA within 7 business days. RCA template fields: timeline, impact, root cause, contributing factors, remediation, owners, follow-up tasks and due dates. Link RCA to incident board and to this playbook.

11) Team wiki & references

- Core repos and pages:
  - infra/networking-configs
  - observability/grafana-dashboards
  - infra/terraform (platform infra)
  - runbooks/incident-templates
  - SLO-registry

- Useful CLI snippets:
  - Check GPU memory on node: kubectl top nodes | grep gpu-node-12
  - Scale inference runtime: kubectl scale deploy/inference-runtime --replicas=10 -n prod
  - Restart stuck consumer: kubectl rollout restart deployment/metrics-consumer -n observability

Closing note: owners are responsible for keeping dashboards accurate, ensuring alerts have clear runbooks, and participating in the Q3 initiatives. If you make alert changes, update the alerts changelog in the observability repo and notify #platform-oncall.

Appendix: example Prometheus alert rule (copy into alerting rules file):

- alert: Inference_HighLatency_P95
  expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(inference_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, model)) > 0.12
  for: 3m
  labels: { severity: "page", team: "serving-runtime" }
  annotations: { summary: "Inference runtime p95 > 120ms for {{ $labels.model }}" }
